title: Gas prices take biggest 3-week dive since 2008 | CNN Business
text:
Source: CNN

Gas prices, a major flashpoint in the midterm election, are collapsing at a historic pace.

The national average for regular gas plunged by 50.5 cents between October 29 and Thursday.

Outside of the 2008 financial crisis, that’s the biggest three-week price drop on record, according to a CNN review of AAA data that goes back to 2000.

“Prices have been in a free-fall,” Patrick De Haan, GasBuddy’s head of petroleum analysis, told CNN.

Pump prices fell by another 3 cents, to $3.72 a gallon, on Thursday. That’s the lowest since March 16.

On a percentage basis, gas prices have tumbled by about 12% between October 29 and Thursday.

It’s the biggest percentage drop since the Covid-19 pandemic lockdowns in early 2020 crashed demand, causing oil and fuel prices to nosedive.

After peaking on October 24, gas prices have declined 26 days in a row through Thursday, the longest streak since the 33-day streak that ended in late June.

First, some of this is driven by the calendar. Demand for gas almost always declines when it gets darker earlier and temperatures drop.

“The colder the weather gets, the less Americans drive,” De Haan said.

Less fuel demand means lower prices at the pump, all else equal.

Secondly, oil futures have retreated from triple-digit territory. Those declines have been driven in part by the fact that the feared reescalation of the Iran war hasn’t happened, at least not yet.

Not only that, but crude continues to exit the Strait of Hormuz – even as the United States and Iran continue to fiercely contest the narrow waterway. This has helped rebuild critical commercial stockpiles in the United States.

Another factor: Refinery outages that caused prices to skyrocket in the Great Lakes region have subsided.

De Haan said gas prices could slide to the mid-$3 range in the coming weeks and months – unless the Iran war seriously heats back up.

“Any sudden reescalation would likely stop or reverse the recent decline. Geopolitics are still the biggest wildcard,” he said.

Of course, gas is not cheap – despite the recent tumble.

The national average of $3.72 a gallon Thursday is well above the year-ago level of $3.09.

Americans have spent anextra $162 billionon gasoline and diesel since the Iran war started, according to research from Brown University. That amounts to more than $1,200 per household.

Despite the recent declines in prices at the pump, this Thanksgiving Day could still mark the most expensive on record for gas. The all-time high was set in 2022 at $3.55 a gallon, according to GasBuddy data.
